title.zh: 記憶體才是那道閘：HBM管制沒有擋住中國做AI晶片，它把自主路線變成一項稅——而稅率不是華府訂的，是2026年記憶體超級循環訂的
title.en: Memory Is the Gate: the HBM Controls Did Not Stop China From Building AI Chips — They Turned Self-Reliance Into a Tax, and Washington Does Not Set the Rate. The 2026 Memory Supercycle Does

focus.zh: 把出口管制當開關是錯的讀法。HBM管制寫在物理參數上（ECCN 3A090.c，每平方毫米2 GB/s），中國因此繞不開、只能繳溢價；而HBM約佔AI加速器製造成本三到四成以上，這筆溢價直接傳導成Ascend 950DT兩個月漲20%到50%。真正少有人講的是第三層：這項稅的稅率由全球記憶體景氣循環決定，不由BIS決定——2026年資料中心吃掉七成以上高階記憶體、標準DRAM合約價單季上修到漲90%到95%，同一份規則文字的咬合力自己變強了。而Huawei用SuperPoD堆到15,488張卡繞過製程限制的同時，也把自己對HBM的需求乘了上去。
focus.en: Treating export control as a switch is the wrong reading. The HBM rule is written against a physical parameter (ECCN 3A090.c, 2 GB/s per square millimetre), so China cannot route around it and must instead pay a premium — and since HBM is roughly 30-45% of an AI accelerator's manufacturing cost, that premium passes straight through, lifting the Ascend 950DT 20-50% in two months. The under-discussed third layer: the rate of this tax is set by the global memory cycle, not by BIS. With data centres absorbing over 70% of high-end memory in 2026 and standard DRAM contract prices revised up to a 90-95% quarterly rise, the same rule text bites harder without a word being changed. And Huawei's SuperPoD route around the fabrication limit — scaling to 15,488 cards — multiplies its own HBM exposure in the process.

title.zh: 「自研HBM」自研的是封裝與控制器，不是DRAM顆粒：Huawei把依賴移位了，卻沒有移除，所以灰市價格照樣傳導到整張加速卡
title.en: Huawei's "Self-Developed HBM" Is Self-Developed at the Packaging and Controller Layer, Not at the DRAM Die — Dependency Relocated, Not Removed, So Grey-Market Prices Still Pass Straight Through to the Card

summary.zh: Huawei的Ascend 950系列對外主打自研高頻寬記憶體HiBL 1.0（128GB、1.6TB/s）與HiZQ 2.0（144GB、4TB/s），表面上看是繞開了美方對HBM的出口管制。但技術層面的實情是：Huawei自研的是2.5D堆疊方式與記憶體控制器，DRAM顆粒本身仍須外部取得。這解釋了9/12報告記錄的那個看似矛盾的現象——一張標榜「自研記憶體」的加速卡，報價卻被HBM灰市行情直接推高：Ascend 950DT兩個月內漲20%到50%、來到人民幣25萬元以上，Cambricon的690漲20%到30%。成本結構讓這條傳導路徑無可迴避：HBM約佔AI加速器製造成本的三到四成以上（Nvidia B200約45%、B100的HBM3E約47%），記憶體與先進封裝合計超過六成BOM。
summary.en: Huawei markets its Ascend 950 line around in-house high-bandwidth memory — HiBL 1.0 (128GB, 1.6TB/s) and HiZQ 2.0 (144GB, 4TB/s) — which reads as a way around US HBM export controls. The technical reality is narrower: what Huawei developed is the 2.5D stacking scheme and the memory controller, while the DRAM dies themselves still have to be sourced externally. That resolves the apparent contradiction logged in 9/12報告, where a card advertised as carrying self-developed memory is nonetheless repriced by the HBM grey market: the Ascend 950DT rose 20-50% in two months to above RMB 250,000, and Cambricon's 690 rose 20-30%. The cost structure makes this pass-through unavoidable: HBM is roughly 30-45% of an AI accelerator's manufacturing cost (about 45% on an Nvidia B200, about 47% HBM3E on a B100), and memory plus advanced packaging exceed 60% of BOM.

implication.zh: 這給你一個判讀中國AI硬體自主進度的具體切分法：不要看廠商說「自研」，要問自研到哪一層。封裝層與控制器層的自研可以很快做到、也很適合對外宣傳，但它不改變顆粒來源，因此不降低受管制曝險；只有DRAM顆粒本身國產化，曝險才會真正下降。用這把尺回頭看，Huawei目前的位置比公開敘事所暗示的更接近「受制於人」而非「已經脫鉤」。對投資判斷而言，這也意味著中國AI晶片廠商的毛利率對全球記憶體報價的敏感度，遠高於一般對「國產替代概念股」的預期——它們的成本曲線其實跟著首爾與美光的報價走。
implication.en: This gives you a usable test for reading China's AI hardware self-sufficiency claims: do not stop at the word "in-house," ask which layer is in-house. Packaging and controller work can be done quickly and markets well, but it does not change where the dies come from and therefore does not reduce exposure to controls. Only domestic DRAM dies reduce that exposure. By that measure Huawei sits closer to "still dependent" than its public narrative implies. For investment purposes it also means Chinese AI chip vendors' margins are far more sensitive to global memory pricing than the usual "domestic substitution play" framing suggests — their cost curves track quotes set in Seoul and Boise.

counterpoint.zh: 反方觀點：這個「移位而非移除」的判斷有明確的到期日。CXMT已於2026年9月進入HBM3E風險量產，樣品正在Alibaba T-Head與Cambricon驗證，最快2027年商用導入；若驗證通過且良率改善，顆粒層的外部依賴會在一到兩年內實質下降，本條的核心論點就會失效。此外，「自研到哪一層」這個分法本身也可能過於嚴格：以產業慣例而言，控制器與堆疊設計本來就是HBM價值鏈中技術門檻最高的環節之一，把它貶為「只是封裝」有低估之嫌。
counterpoint.en: Counterpoint: this "relocated, not removed" judgement has a dated expiry. CXMT entered HBM3E risk production in September 2026, with samples in qualification at Alibaba's T-Head and Cambricon and possible commercial integration as early as 2027. If qualification passes and yields improve, external die-layer dependency falls materially within one to two years and this item's core claim expires with it. The layer test may also be too strict on its own terms: controller and stack design are among the harder parts of the HBM value chain, and dismissing them as "just packaging" understates the work.

items.source: Reuters 9/10 獨家報導（Huawei、Cambricon 報價）；TrendForce 3/23 報導 Huawei 自研 HBM 規格；成本結構估計來自 SiliconAnalysts 與 DIGITIMES

title.zh: 台灣同時是先進封裝的單點、管制清單的執行者與走私案的起訴地：CoWoS約佔全球AI先進封裝九成，5/21辦出第一起AI硬體走私刑事案
title.en: Taiwan Is Simultaneously the Single Point of Advanced Packaging, an Enforcer of Control Lists, and the Venue of the First Smuggling Prosecution — CoWoS Holds About 90% of Global AI Advanced Packaging, and the Island's First Criminal Case Landed 5/21

summary.zh: 在這套以記憶體與封裝為核心的管制結構裡，台灣佔據三個同時成立的位置。第一，TSMC的CoWoS約佔全球AI晶片先進封裝的九成，連在美國亞利桑那廠製造的晶片目前仍運回台灣完成封裝。第二，台灣經濟部國際貿易署於2025/9/18將279個實體增列進戰略性高科技貨品（SHTC）管制名單，對象主要位於中國、伊朗與巴基斯坦，並規劃再增列先進半導體設備、先進3D列印設備與量子電腦等18項貨品。第三，2026/5/21台灣執行首起針對AI硬體非法出口的刑事偵辦行動，搜索12處地點，對包含Supermicro共同創辦人Wally Liaw在內的三人聲請羈押，涉嫌以偽造文件將搭載Nvidia晶片的伺服器輸往中國、香港與澳門。
summary.en: In a control architecture built around memory and packaging, Taiwan occupies three positions at once. First, TSMC's CoWoS accounts for roughly 90% of global advanced packaging for AI chips — even dies fabricated at the Arizona plant currently return to Taiwan to be packaged. Second, Taiwan's International Trade Administration added 279 entities to its Strategic High-Tech Commodities (SHTC) control list on 2025/9/18, predominantly in China, Iran and Pakistan, and moved to add 18 further item categories covering advanced semiconductor equipment, advanced 3D printing equipment and quantum computers. Third, on 2026/5/21 Taiwan executed its first criminal enforcement action against illegal AI hardware exports, searching 12 locations and seeking detention of three people including Supermicro co-founder Wally Liaw, over allegedly using forged documentation to route Nvidia-equipped servers to China, Hong Kong and Macau.

implication.zh: 這改變了你在跟外國對話者討論台灣角色時該用的措辭。常見的框架把台灣描述成「配合美方管制的盟友」，但實際結構是：沒有台灣的封裝產能與執法動作，這套管制在物理上與程序上都難以執行——台灣是節點，不是配角。這個定位同時給了台北籌碼與風險：籌碼在於先進封裝的不可替代性短期內無解；風險在於高度集中本身就是對手最值得攻擊的單點，而且這個單點的價值會隨著HBM4世代（記憶體加封裝佔BOM比重續升）而更高。對你評估台灣供應鏈個股，這也指向一個具體的追蹤對象：能合法對非中國市場供應先進封裝、基板與測試產能的業者，正處在全球缺口的核心。
implication.en: This should change how you frame Taiwan's role in conversation with foreign counterparts. The common framing casts Taiwan as "an ally cooperating with US controls." The structural reality is that without Taiwanese packaging capacity and Taiwanese enforcement action, the regime is neither physically nor procedurally enforceable — Taiwan is the node, not a supporting actor. That position carries both leverage and risk: the leverage is that advanced packaging has no near-term substitute; the risk is that such concentration is exactly the single point an adversary would target, and its value rises further with the HBM4 generation as memory-plus-packaging climbs as a share of BOM. For Taiwanese equity exposure it points at a concrete watchlist: firms that can lawfully supply advanced packaging, substrate and test capacity to non-China markets sit at the centre of the global gap.

items.source: 台灣經濟部國際貿易署 2025/9/18 SHTC 增列公告（OpenSanctions 收錄原始資料集）；2026/5/21 台灣檢調首起 AI 硬體走私偵辦行動，經 Taiwan News、Taipei Times 等報導

title.zh: 管制寫在物理參數上而不是公司名上：ECCN 3A090.c以「每平方毫米2 GB/s」畫線，於是規避也只能沿著這條參數的幾何走
title.en: The Control Is Written Against a Physical Parameter, Not a Company Name: ECCN 3A090.c Draws the Line at 2 GB/s per Square Millimetre — So Evasion Can Only Follow That Parameter's Geometry

summary.zh: 美國商務部工業與安全局（BIS）2024/12/5的規則把HBM納入商品管制清單ECCN 3A090.c，門檻定為「memory bandwidth density（記憶體頻寬密度）大於每平方毫米2 GB/s」，並透過EAR §734.9(h)的先進運算外國直接產品規則（FDPR），把符合條件的非美製HBM堆疊一併納管；同時設立License Exception HBM，允許出貨到美國或盟國總部企業所有的封裝廠、並要求追蹤送出與送回的數量。多數條文於2024/12/31生效。BIS給出的理由是HBM為先進運算IC生產過程的重要環節，提供AI模型與超級運算所需的記憶體容量與頻寬。公開分析指出這個寫法產生兩個具體後果：規則管制的是裸堆疊，並未涵蓋已整合進AI晶片的HBM，2024年底至2025年初出現把Samsung HBM草率貼附於極簡處理器晶片後出口的操作；且規則內容在生效前約半年即外洩，使Huawei得以預先囤積約一年份的HBM。
summary.en: The Bureau of Industry and Security's 2024/12/5 rule placed HBM on the Commerce Control List under ECCN 3A090.c at a threshold of "memory bandwidth density greater than 2 gigabytes per second per square millimetre," and used the Advanced Computing Foreign Direct Product Rule at EAR §734.9(h) to sweep in qualifying non-US-made stacks. It also created License Exception HBM, permitting transfers to packaging sites owned by US- or allied-headquartered companies provided the company tracks quantities sent and returned. Most provisions took effect 2024/12/31. BIS's stated rationale is that HBM stacks are an important part of producing advanced computing ICs and supply the memory capacity and bandwidth AI models and supercomputing require. Published analysis identifies two concrete consequences of drafting it this way: the rule covers bare stacks but not HBM already integrated into an AI chip, and in late 2024 and early 2025 several Taiwanese firms reportedly exploited that by loosely attaching Samsung HBM to very simple processor dies before export; and the rule leaked roughly six months before it took effect, allowing Huawei to stockpile about a year's worth of HBM in advance.

implication.zh: 參數化管制的優缺點是一體兩面，值得你在跟政策圈對話時直接指出來。優點是抗規避：不點名公司，所以換殼、換代理商、換第三國都不改變門檻，這是它比實體清單更耐用的地方。缺點是規避的形狀完全可預測——攻擊面就在參數定義的邊界上。這推出一個一般性原則：任何以技術門檻定義的管制，其漏洞必然出現在「門檻怎麼量、量在哪一層」的定義縫隙裡，而不是出現在執法強度上。對威脅獵捕與provenance建模的類比也成立：當你用一個量化門檻定義「異常」，對手的最優策略永遠是把行為調整到門檻的另一側，而不是提升隱匿技術。
implication.en: The strengths and weaknesses of parameter-based control are the same property viewed twice, and it is worth naming directly in policy conversation. The strength is evasion resistance: because no company is named, re-badging, swapping intermediaries and rerouting through third countries leave the threshold untouched — which is why it outlasts entity listings. The weakness is that the shape of evasion becomes entirely predictable, because the attack surface sits exactly on the boundary the parameter defines. The general principle follows: any control defined by a technical threshold will leak at the seams of how the threshold is measured and at which layer, not at the level of enforcement effort. The analogy carries into threat hunting and provenance modelling: when you define "anomalous" by a quantitative threshold, an adversary's optimal move is always to sit on the other side of that threshold rather than to improve concealment.

items.source: BIS 2024/12/5 interim final rule（聯邦公報 2024-28270，ECCN 3A090.c、License Exception HBM，2024/12/31 生效）；規避手法與洩漏時序見 AI Frontiers 專文分析

title.zh: SuperPoD的反效果：Huawei公開承認單晶片落後、主張用互連在系統層補回來——但堆到15,488張卡，等於把自己對HBM的需求乘上去
title.en: The SuperPoD Backfire: Huawei Openly Concedes Its Single Chips Lag and Argues the Gap Closes at System Level Through Interconnect — but Scaling to 15,488 Cards Multiplies Its Own HBM Exposure

summary.zh: Huawei副董事長Xu Zhijun在公開發表的三年晶片路線圖（910C於2025年、950PR與950DT於2026年、960於2027年、970於2028年）中明確承認：因受制裁而無法在TSMC製造，單晶片效能落後Nvidia，因此重押互連技術，用數以萬計的卡組成超節點（SuperPoD），在系統層交付最強算力。Atlas 950 SuperPoD規模為8,192張卡，Atlas 960規劃於2027年達到15,488張卡。Xu明言此舉旨在「繞過中國晶片製造製程的限制」。這個推理在運算層面成立，但它與記憶體約束的互動方向是相反的：以更多張卡累加算力，每一張卡都要配置自己的HBM堆疊，總HBM需求因此隨卡數等比放大，而非縮減。
summary.en: In a publicly presented three-year roadmap (910C in 2025, 950PR and 950DT in 2026, 960 in 2027, 970 in 2028), Huawei deputy chairman Xu Zhijun explicitly concedes that sanctions bar the company from manufacturing at TSMC and that its single-chip performance trails Nvidia's, and that Huawei therefore bet heavily on interconnect, assembling tens of thousands of cards into SuperPoDs to deliver leading compute at system level. The Atlas 950 SuperPoD spans 8,192 cards; the Atlas 960 is planned to reach 15,488 cards in 2027. Xu states the aim is to circumvent the limits of China's chip manufacturing processes. The compute reasoning holds, but its interaction with the memory constraint runs the other way: aggregating performance across more cards requires each card to carry its own HBM stack, so total HBM demand scales up with card count rather than down.

implication.zh: 這是本期最值得你帶進對談的一句話：中國繞過製程限制的那條路，正好是最吃記憶體的那條路。它推翻了「中國會用系統設計把管制消化掉」這個常見樂觀論——系統設計確實能消化製程劣勢，但它是用記憶體換來的，而記憶體正是目前被卡得最緊的那一層。對政策圈的意義是，若華府的目標是壓制中國可用算力總量，那麼強化HBM管制的邊際效果會高於強化製程設備管制，因為叢集路線讓前者的槓桿隨規模放大。對你判斷實際算力的意義則是：評估中國AI算力時，與其追蹤晶片製程節點，不如追蹤它一年能拿到多少顆HBM堆疊——那才是綁住總量的變數。
implication.en: This is the sentence worth carrying into conversation: China's route around the fabrication constraint is precisely its most memory-hungry route. It undercuts the common optimistic claim that clever system design will absorb the controls. System design does absorb the process disadvantage — but it pays for that in memory, and memory is the layer currently squeezed hardest. For policymakers the implication is that if the objective is to cap China's usable aggregate compute, tightening HBM controls has higher marginal effect than tightening fabrication equipment controls, because the cluster strategy makes the former's leverage scale with size. For your own estimates the implication is sharper still: when sizing Chinese AI compute, tracking how many HBM stacks the country can obtain in a year tells you more than tracking process nodes, because that is the variable binding the total.

counterpoint.zh: 反方觀點：這條推論假設每張卡的HBM配置維持不變，但這不必然成立。若Huawei為叢集場景設計降規記憶體配置（較低容量、較低頻寬、但靠互連頻寬補償），單卡HBM用量可以下降，總需求未必等比放大。此外，把HBM堆疊數當成算力總量的代理指標，也忽略了利用率這個變數——推論與訓練的記憶體綁定程度差異很大，同樣數量的HBM在推論場景能支撐的實際工作負載遠高於訓練場景，而中國目前的部署重心明顯偏向推論。
counterpoint.en: Counterpoint: this reasoning assumes per-card HBM configuration stays constant, which need not hold. If Huawei specifies reduced memory for cluster deployments — lower capacity and bandwidth, compensated by interconnect bandwidth — per-card HBM consumption falls and aggregate demand need not scale proportionally. Using HBM stack count as a proxy for aggregate compute also ignores utilisation: inference and training bind memory very differently, the same quantity of HBM supports far more real workload in inference than in training, and China's deployment weight currently sits clearly on the inference side.

items.source: Huawei Connect 上 Xu Zhijun 公開發表之晶片路線圖與 Atlas SuperPoD 規格，經 SCMP 與 China Daily 各自獨立報導；規模數字取自同一份公開發表

title.zh: 國產顆粒的真實高度：CXMT於9月進入HBM3E風險量產、樣品送驗T-Head與Cambricon，但HBM3八層堆疊整體良率模型僅約25%
title.en: How High the Domestic Die Bar Actually Sits: CXMT Entered HBM3E Risk Production in September with Samples in Qualification at T-Head and Cambricon — but Modelled Overall Yield on Eight-High HBM3 Stacks Is Only About 25%

summary.zh: 中國最大DRAM廠CXMT（長鑫存儲）已於2026年9月啟動HBM3E風險量產，並將樣品送交Alibaba旗下T-Head與Cambricon進行驗證，最快可能於2027年進入商用整合。產能規劃方面，CXMT預計將HBM3產線配置為月產約6萬片晶圓，約佔其2026年總產能30萬片的兩成；另有估計認為中國2026年可產出約700萬顆HBM3 die，約足以支撐600,000顆H100等級的AI晶片。但良率仍是主要限制：SemiAnalysis於2026年6月的模型顯示，CXMT的HBM3八層堆疊前段良率約35%、後段約70%，整體約25%；The Information亦報導CXMT持續受低良率所困。其HBM供給同時受後段產能與封裝環節限制，包括堆疊組裝、鍵合、翹曲控制與封裝良率學習曲線。
summary.en: CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies), China's largest DRAM maker, began HBM3E risk production in September 2026 and delivered samples to Alibaba's T-Head division and to Cambricon for qualification, with possible commercial integration as early as 2027. On capacity, CXMT plans roughly 60,000 wafers per month on its HBM3 line, about 20% of its 300,000 wafer monthly total for 2026; separate estimates put Chinese output at roughly 7 million HBM3 dies in 2026, enough for about 600,000 H100-class AI chips. Yield remains the binding limit: SemiAnalysis modelled CXMT's eight-high HBM3 stack yield in June 2026 at about 35% front-end and 70% back-end, roughly 25% overall, and The Information reported continuing low-yield problems. CXMT's HBM supply is additionally constrained at the back end — stacking and assembly, bonding, warpage control, and a slow package yield learning curve.

implication.zh: 這條是本期主論證的到期時鐘，值得單獨追蹤而不是併進背景。25%整體良率的意思是：能做出來，但每一顆可用顆粒的實際成本是理論值的四倍左右，因此短期內國產顆粒不會壓低Huawei與Cambricon的成本曲線——它先解決「有沒有」，還沒解決「貴不貴」。你要盯的轉折點不是「CXMT宣布量產」這種公告，而是兩個更難造假的訊號：一是T-Head與Cambricon是否真的在量產機種上採用（驗證通過與商用導入是兩回事），二是Huawei與Cambricon的報價是否開始回落。前者若在2027上半年出現，代表本期「顆粒層依賴仍在」的判斷提前失效。
implication.en: This item is the expiry clock on this week's main argument and deserves separate tracking rather than relegation to background. A 25% overall yield means the part can be built, but each usable die costs roughly four times its theoretical cost — so domestic dies will not flatten Huawei's or Cambricon's cost curves in the near term. They solve availability before they solve price. The turning point to watch is not a mass-production announcement, which is cheap to make, but two signals that are harder to fake: whether T-Head and Cambricon actually design the part into shipping products (passing qualification and reaching commercial integration are different events), and whether Huawei and Cambricon quotes begin to fall. If the first appears in H1 2027, this week's judgement that die-layer dependency persists expires early.

counterpoint.zh: 反方觀點：用25%良率推斷成本劣勢可能高估了瓶頸高度。記憶體產業的良率學習曲線歷來下降得非常快，而CXMT是在有國家資源支撐、且不必對外部股東交代短期毛利的條件下推進——它可以承受長時間的低良率量產來換取學習曲線，這與商業廠商的決策邏輯不同。此外，SemiAnalysis的數字是模型推估而非CXMT實測揭露，The Information的報導亦屬單一來源；若實際良率已高於模型值，本條對時程的判斷會整體偏保守。
counterpoint.en: Counterpoint: inferring a cost disadvantage from a 25% yield may overstate the height of the bottleneck. Memory yield learning curves have historically fallen fast, and CXMT is advancing with state backing and without having to answer to outside shareholders on near-term margin — it can absorb prolonged low-yield production to buy down the learning curve, which is not how a commercial supplier would decide. The SemiAnalysis figures are also modelled estimates rather than disclosed measurements, and The Information's reporting is single-source; if actual yields already exceed the model, this item's timeline judgement is systematically too conservative.

items.source: The Information 首報 CXMT HBM3E 風險量產，經 Korea JoongAng Daily 等獨立轉述；良率數字來自 SemiAnalysis 2026 年 6 月 CXMT 深度分析模型；產能規劃數字來自產業媒體彙整

title.zh: 合法管道開了，北京不走：H200自1/15改為逐案審查、25%抽成、每家75,000顆上限，約十家中企獲准，但Commerce官員7/14告訴國會出貨「極少」
title.en: The Legal Channel Opened and Beijing Declined to Use It: Since 1/15 the H200 Moved to Case-by-Case Review With a 25% Cut and a 75,000-Unit Cap, About Ten Chinese Firms Were Approved — and a Commerce Official Told Congress on 7/14 Shipments Were "Very Few"

summary.zh: 美國商務部於2026/1/15發布最終規則，將Nvidia H200與AMD MI325X對中國的出口許可審查從推定拒絕改為逐案審查，附帶條件包括25%的收入分成或關稅、數量上限、第三方測試與嚴格的KYC要求。商務部隨後核准約十家中國企業採購H200（包括Alibaba、Tencent與ByteDance），每家上限75,000顆。但實際結果是：Nvidia雖持有對這約十家企業的銷售許可，幾乎沒有實際出貨，一名商務部官員於2026/7/14向國會表示出貨量「極少」。與此同時，9/10報告記錄的另一條線索顯示北京要求境內大廠避開已獲核准的Nvidia晶片。兩者合起來構成一個不尋常的狀態：美方願意賣、並已設計好抽成機制，中方不買。
summary.en: On 2026/1/15 the Commerce Department issued a final rule moving export licence review for Nvidia's H200 and AMD's MI325X to China from presumption of denial to case-by-case review, conditioned on a 25% revenue share or tariff, volume caps, third-party testing and strict KYC requirements. Commerce subsequently cleared about ten Chinese firms — including Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance — to purchase the H200, capped at 75,000 units each. The outcome, however, is that while Nvidia holds licences covering those firms, almost nothing has shipped: a Commerce official told Congress on 2026/7/14 that shipments were "very few." Alongside this, the thread logged in 9/10報告 indicates Beijing has directed major domestic firms to avoid approved Nvidia parts. Together these produce an unusual configuration: Washington is willing to sell and has built a mechanism to take a cut, and Beijing is not buying.

implication.zh: 這條把本期的主論證補完：中國廠商付的那項「記憶體稅」，有一部分是自願承擔的。如果單純按成本效益計算，採購已獲核准的H200會比用灰市HBM自製加速卡便宜得多；北京選擇不走這條路，代表它把供應鏈自主的政治價值定得高於當期成本。對你的判讀有兩個後果。其一，不要用市場化的價格訊號去預測中國的採購行為——政治考量會持續壓抑本該出現的套利。其二，這也讓美方的管制目標變得模糊：當華府同時願意收租售賣高階晶片、又封鎖HBM，它實質上是在補貼中國走那條更貴、更慢、但更自主的路。若目標是延緩中國AI能力，這個組合未必是最優解。
implication.en: This completes the week's main argument: part of the memory tax Chinese vendors pay is self-imposed. On pure cost-benefit terms, buying approved H200s would be markedly cheaper than building accelerators around grey-market HBM. Beijing declining that route means it prices supply-chain autonomy above current cost. Two consequences follow. First, do not use market price signals to predict Chinese procurement — political weighting will keep suppressing arbitrage that should otherwise appear. Second, it blurs what Washington's controls are for: by simultaneously agreeing to sell high-end chips for a cut and blocking HBM, the US is in effect subsidising China's more expensive, slower, more autonomous path. If the objective is to delay Chinese AI capability, that combination is not obviously the optimum.

counterpoint.zh: 反方觀點：把出貨稀少完全歸因於北京的政治指導，可能過度推論。至少三個非政治性解釋同時存在且未被排除——其一，Nvidia自身產能在HBM4世代同樣吃緊，對中國訂單的優先順序本就偏低；其二，逐案審查加上第三方測試與嚴格KYC流程，本身就會使實際交付週期遠長於許可核發；其三，25%的抽成直接推高終端價格，可能使H200對中國買家的性價比不如帳面。若主因是後三者而非政治指導，那麼「中國自願付稅」這個判斷就不成立，本條的推論要整條收回。
counterpoint.en: Counterpoint: attributing thin shipments entirely to Beijing's political guidance likely over-reads the evidence. At least three non-political explanations remain live and unexcluded. First, Nvidia's own capacity is equally tight through the HBM4 generation, so China orders would sit low in its allocation priority regardless. Second, case-by-case review plus third-party testing and strict KYC procedures lengthen actual delivery cycles far beyond licence issuance. Third, the 25% cut raises the landed price directly, potentially making the H200 less attractive to Chinese buyers than the headline suggests. If those explanations dominate rather than political direction, the claim that China is voluntarily paying the tax fails and this item's inference should be withdrawn entirely.

items.source: BIS 2026/1/15 最終規則（H200／MI325X 改逐案審查，附 25% 收入分成、數量上限、第三方測試與 KYC 條件）與商務部官員 2026/7/14 國會說明，經 TechPowerUp 等科技媒體轉述彙整

narrative.zh:
**上期推演校準**

9/7週報留下四條指標，一週後誠實的答案是：一條方向被補強但我的指標抓不到，三條仍未定，零條被推翻。第二條（是否出現第一起授時側事故）沒有出現導航以外的事故，但9/12報告記錄的StyleSmuggler把C2心跳偽裝成NTP流量，是同一弱點的另一面——我只想到「時鐘會漂」，沒想到「時間通道本身會被當成掩護」。方向站得住，指標太窄。其餘三條無新事證：波蘭數據要到冬季，RTS 25揭露與Xona Pulsar採購都沒動靜，CCW第七次審查會議11/16-20還沒開。

真正該記下的錯不在哪一條，而在我把四條全寫成三到六個月才會動的指標，等於讓自己一週後無事可對。更該警惕的是形狀：9/7週報說「西方補丁到位前有一個窗口」，本期我又要寫一個窗口。連續兩週把世界解釋成同一個形狀，比任何單一判斷出錯更危險。

**問題是什麼**

9/12報告記了一條價格訊號：Huawei的Ascend 950DT報價拉到人民幣25萬元以上，兩個月漲20%到50%，Cambricon的690漲20%到30%，原因都指向HBM成本。常見讀法是「管制奏效，中國被卡住了」——這錯在把出口管制當成開關。真正發生的是：管制沒有擋住中國做出AI晶片，它把自主路線變成一項稅，而稅率不是華府訂的。

**機制怎麼運作**

第一層，管制寫在物理參數上。2024年12月的規則把HBM放進ECCN 3A090.c，門檻是「memory bandwidth density大於每平方毫米2 GB/s」，再用FDPR把非美製堆疊納管。好處是換公司、換第三國都不改變門檻；代價是規避只能沿著參數的幾何走——規則管裸堆疊、不管已整合進AI晶片的HBM，於是出現把Samsung HBM貼到無用處理器上再出口的操作。規則又在生效前半年外洩，Huawei因此先囤了約一年份。

第二層，依賴被移位而非移除。Huawei的「自研HBM」自研的是2.5D堆疊與控制器，不是DRAM顆粒；顆粒仍要外求，灰市價格照樣傳導。而HBM約佔AI加速器製造成本三到四成以上（B200約45%），記憶體加先進封裝超過六成BOM。卡在記憶體，就是卡在整張卡。

第三層才是重點：稅率由全球記憶體景氣循環決定，不由BIS決定。2026年資料中心吃掉七成以上高階記憶體，標準DRAM合約價第一季季增被上修到90%到95%，SK hynix新產能要2028到2029才進來。同一份規則文字，在寬鬆市場裡只是溢價，在超級循環裡是數倍。華府一個字沒改，咬合力自己變強了。

**證據**

最能說明第三層的，是Huawei自己的解法加深了曝險。Xu Zhijun公開承認單晶片落後，主張靠互連在系統層補回來：Atlas 950 SuperPoD堆到8,192張卡，2027年要到15,488張。但堆卡不會減少HBM需求，它把需求乘上去——繞過製程限制的那條路，正好最吃記憶體。

反向證據也要放進來：CXMT已於2026年9月進入HBM3E風險量產，樣品送Alibaba T-Head與Cambricon驗證。但SemiAnalysis模型顯示其HBM3八層堆疊整體良率約25%——做得出來，還做不便宜。

**各方自己怎麼說**

華府說HBM是先進運算IC生產的重要環節，管制是為拖慢中國AI晶片產能。最有力的一點是參數化：不點名公司，換殼無效。最不願被追問的是2026/1/15的轉向——H200改逐案審查、25%抽成、每家75,000顆上限，約十家中企獲准，等於承認目的已從「阻斷」滑向「收租與計量」。

北京說自主可控，且不否認單晶片落後——它主張計量單位該是叢集而非晶片，直接挑戰美方用單晶片參數畫線的方法論。最不願被追問的是：叢集路線把HBM總需求乘上去，而國產良率還在25%。

首爾最尷尬：SK hynix在中國有三座廠卻不准在當地賣最先進HBM，美方2025年撤掉VEU、改成逐年許可。韓方最在意的是規劃週期比一個折舊年度還短。

台北同時站三個位置：CoWoS約佔全球AI先進封裝九成、2025/9/18增列279個實體、2026/5/21辦出第一起AI硬體走私刑事案。台灣不是旁觀者，是這套管制能否執行的實體節點——而這種集中既是最大籌碼，也是最大單點風險。

**未來 3–6 個月的推演與觀察指標**

主判斷：2026下半到2027是咬合力最強的一段，因為它同時領到「管制」與「全球缺貨」兩份力量，而兩者到期時間不同：缺貨等2028到2029新產能，國產顆粒最快2027。五條可證偽指標：一、Ascend 950DT報價若在2027年第一季前回落到人民幣20萬元以下，我「灰市溢價是結構性」的判斷就錯了。二、CXMT HBM3E是否在2027上半年商用導入；若成真，顆粒層依賴消解快我一年。三、H200實際出貨——Commerce官員7/14告訴國會出貨「極少」，若2027年前明顯放量，北京的不買指導就鬆了。四、Samsung與SK hynix中國廠年度許可是否在12/31前續發——不續發代表管制從管產品升級到管產能。五、看TSMC法說10/15與Nvidia財報11/25對CoWoS與HBM4的口徑。

**我可能錯在哪**

最可能錯的是我把「窗口」這個形狀用上癮了。窗口論假設對手會理性地在窗口內把壓力最大化，但真實採購決策更常是慣性的、被預算年度切割的。如果Huawei只是照原訂節奏出貨，而灰市溢價其實只是全球缺貨的一部分、與管制關係不大，整個「稅率由循環決定」的論證就塌了。這個反駁很有力：2026年全世界的記憶體買家都在漲價。要分辨只有一個辦法——看價差而不是看價格：中國境內HBM相對境外的倍數若隨全球缺貨同步收斂，管制那一份力量其實很小。

第二個可能的錯在我對CXMT的折算。我用25%良率推論「還做不便宜」，但記憶體業良率曲線歷來下降很快，且已有估計認為中國2026年可產出約700萬顆HBM3 die，約支撐600,000顆H100級晶片。若這數字接近真實，瓶頸比我畫的低不少，「稅」這個比喻就下得太重。
narrative.en:
**Calibrating Last Week's Forecasts**

The 9/7週報 left four indicators. One week on: one reinforced in direction but missed by my own metric, three open, none overturned. No timing-side incident surfaced — but StyleSmuggler in 9/12報告, disguising C2 heartbeats as NTP traffic, is the same weakness from the other side: I had imagined clocks drifting, not the timing channel used as cover. The rest show nothing yet; CCW convenes 11/16-20.

The deeper error: I wrote all four to move over three to six months, leaving nothing to check a week later. And the shape repeats — the 9/7週報 argued a window before Western fixes land, this week another. That worries me more than any single wrong call.

**The Question**

9/12報告 logged a price signal: Huawei's Ascend 950DT quotes above RMB 250,000, up 20-50% in two months; Cambricon's 690 up 20-30%. Both point at HBM costs. The standard reading — "controls are working, China is blocked" — treats export control as a switch. What actually happened: the controls did not stop China building AI chips; they turned self-reliance into a tax, and Washington does not set the rate.

**How the Mechanism Works**

First, the control is written against a physical parameter: ECCN 3A090.c, "memory bandwidth density greater than 2 GB/s per square millimetre," with the FDPR sweeping in non-US-made stacks. The threshold survives any change of company or transit country; the cost is that evasion follows the parameter's geometry — the rule covers bare stacks, not HBM already inside an AI chip, hence the reported practice of attaching Samsung HBM to throwaway dies before export. It leaked six months early, letting Huawei stockpile a year's supply.

Second, dependency was relocated, not removed. Huawei's "self-developed HBM" is self-developed at the stacking and controller layer, not at the DRAM die — the dies still come from outside, so grey-market pricing passes through. HBM is 30-45% of an accelerator's manufacturing cost, memory plus packaging above 60% of BOM.

Third, the point: the tax rate is set by the global memory cycle, not by BIS. Data centres absorb over 70% of high-end memory in 2026; standard DRAM contract prices were revised up to a 90-95% quarterly rise; SK hynix capacity arrives only in 2028-2029. The same text is a mild premium in a loose market and a multiple in a supercycle — Washington changed nothing and the bite strengthened by itself.

**Evidence**

Huawei's own workaround deepens its exposure. Xu Zhijun concedes single-chip performance lags and closes the gap through interconnect: the Atlas 950 SuperPoD spans 8,192 cards, reaching 15,488 by 2027. But stacking cards multiplies HBM demand rather than reducing it — the route around the fabrication limit is the most memory-hungry available.

Counter-evidence: CXMT entered HBM3E risk production in September 2026, with samples at Alibaba's T-Head and Cambricon. But SemiAnalysis models its eight-high HBM3 yield near 25% — they can build it, not yet cheaply.

**How Each Side Tells It**

Washington calls HBM an important part of producing advanced computing ICs; its strongest point is parameterisation — no company named, so re-badging fails. What it least wants pressed is the 2026/1/15 pivot: the H200 moved to case-by-case review with a 25% cut and a 75,000-unit cap, conceding the objective slid from denial toward metering.

Beijing says self-reliance and does not dispute that its chips lag — it argues the unit of measurement is the cluster, not the chip, attacking the whole methodology of single-chip thresholds. What it least wants pressed is that this multiplies HBM demand while domestic yields sit near 25%.

Seoul is most awkwardly placed: SK hynix runs three China fabs yet cannot sell leading-edge HBM there, and Washington replaced VEU status with annual licences — a planning horizon shorter than one depreciation cycle.

Taipei holds three positions: roughly 90% of AI advanced packaging through CoWoS, 279 entities added on 2025/9/18, and its first smuggling prosecution on 2026/5/21. Taiwan is the node determining whether the regime is enforceable — concentration that is both its greatest leverage and its greatest vulnerability.

**Forecasts and Indicators for the Next 3-6 Months**

Core judgement: late 2026 through 2027 is the period of maximum bite, because regulation and scarcity apply at once but expire on different clocks — scarcity waits for 2028-2029 capacity, domestic dies arrive 2027 at the earliest. Five falsifiable indicators. One: if the Ascend 950DT falls below RMB 200,000 before Q1 2027, my structural-premium claim is wrong. Two: whether CXMT's HBM3E reaches commercial integration in H1 2027. Three: H200 shipments — Commerce told Congress on 7/14 they were "very few"; a clear ramp means Beijing's guidance loosened. Four: whether Samsung's and SK hynix's China licences are renewed before 12/31 — non-renewal escalates from controlling products to controlling capacity. Five: TSMC on 10/15 and Nvidia on 11/25 on CoWoS and HBM4.

**Where I Could Be Wrong**

The likeliest error is addiction to the "window" shape, which assumes adversaries rationally maximise pressure inside it, whereas real procurement is inertial and cut up by budget years. If Huawei is simply shipping on its original cadence and the premium is mostly global shortage, the argument collapses — every memory buyer on earth is paying more in 2026. So watch the spread, not the price: if the multiple between HBM inside and outside China converges with global scarcity, the regulatory component is small.

Second, my arithmetic on CXMT. I inferred "not yet cheaply" from a 25% yield, but memory yield curves improve fast, and one estimate puts Chinese output at roughly 7 million HBM3 dies in 2026 — enough for about 600,000 H100-class chips. If so, the bottleneck is lower than I drew it and "tax" is too heavy a metaphor.
